source_text: Ad bonum fecunditatis parvulos pertinere, quae Dei benedictione ante morbum libidinis instituta est; non ad ipsum libidinis morbum, si postea peccantibus accidit; atque ideo sanctitatem adscribendam esse nascentibus, et generantibus culpam
pass_a_gloss: To good of-fruitfulness parvulos pertinere, which of-God by-blessing before sickness of-lust instituta is; not to itself of-lust sickness, if afterward peccantibus accidit; and for-that-reason sanctitatem adscribendam to-be nascentibus, and generantibus fault.

lemmas.lexica: LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Infants belong to the good of fruitfulness, which God’s blessing established before the disease of desire, not to the disease of desire itself, if that arose afterward when people sinned. Therefore holiness must be ascribed to those born, and guilt to those who conceive them.

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
